title: Kay Hagan Tick Act Reauthorization
official_title: To reauthorize the Kay Hagan Tick Act, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Introduced by Rep. Christopher H. Smith (R-NJ-4) with 36 cosponsors, and passed the House per the latest recorded action after referral to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce. The measure is a short window-shift reauthorization of two Public Health Service Act authorities that expired at the end of fiscal year 2025 — the kind of bipartisan public-health reauthorization that typically clears the Senate. The introduced-clause change replacing the specific reference to the "Tick-Borne Disease Working Group" with "appropriate individuals" removes a statutorily named consultation body and could draw questions in the Senate HELP Committee, though not enough to derail a broadly cosponsored measure.
summary: Section 317U of the Public Health Service Act authorizes a national strategy and regional Centers of Excellence in Vector-Borne Disease at CDC to identify, report, prevent, and respond to vector-borne diseases including tick-borne illnesses; section 2822 authorizes enhanced support to help state and local health departments address vector-borne diseases. Both authorizations lapsed at the end of fiscal year 2025 — this bill reauthorizes them for fiscal years 2026 through 2030, and also replaces the requirement that CDC consult with the statutorily named "Tick-Borne Disease Working Group" with a broader requirement to consult with "appropriate individuals", and adds language requiring the national strategy to address the underlying capacity of state and local health departments to identify, report, prevent, and respond to such diseases.
brief: Reauthorizes both authorities of the Kay Hagan Tick Act — the CDC-led National Strategy and Regional Centers of Excellence in Vector-Borne Disease, and enhanced support to health departments — for fiscal years 2026 through 2030.

top_lines.headline: Vector-Borne Disease Authorities Reauthorized
subs: Section 317U of the Public Health Service Act reauthorized through FY2030
Section 2822 (enhanced support for health departments) reauthorized through FY2030

top_lines.headline: Consultation Language Change
subs: Removes the statutorily named Tick-Borne Disease Working Group as a required consultee, leaving only a general "appropriate individuals" requirement

top_lines.headline: Strategy Scope Clarified
subs: National strategy must address increasing capacity to identify, report, prevent, and respond to vector-borne diseases
Language inserted into the existing "activities of the Centers" list

items.main: Reauthorizes Section 317U of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 247b-23) — the National Strategy and Regional Centers of Excellence in Vector-Borne Disease — for fiscal years 2026 through 2030.
items.detail: Amends subsection (f) of Section 317U by striking "2021 through 2025" and inserting "2026 through 2030". Amends subsection (b) by striking the reference to the "Tick-Borne Disease Working Group established under section 2062 of the 21st Century Cures Act (42 U.S.C. 284s) and other individuals, as appropriate" and inserting "appropriate individuals". Amends subsection (c)(4) by inserting ", including by increasing capacity to identify, report, prevent, and respond to such diseases" before the period at the end.

items.main: Reauthorizes Section 2822 of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 300hh-32) — Enhanced Support To Assist Health Departments in Addressing Vector-Borne Diseases — for fiscal years 2026 through 2030.
items.detail: Amends Section 2822(c) by striking "2021 through 2025" and inserting "2026 through 2030". No dollar figure is changed; the authorization window is shifted forward by five fiscal years.

underreported.summary: The bill strikes the specific reference to the Tick-Borne Disease Working Group (established under section 2062 of the 21st Century Cures Act, 42 U.S.C. 284s) from the CDC consultation requirement and replaces it with the general phrase "appropriate individuals".
underreported.why_unreported: The section is captioned "Reauthorization of Programs" but this operative change removes a statutorily named consultation body — a substantive policy change unrelated to the reauthorization window.

gaps: The bill reauthorizes both PHS Act authorities for FY2026-FY2030 but does not set any dollar amount — reauthorization sets an authorization ceiling only in years where a subsequent appropriations act names one.

The bill strikes the requirement to consult the Tick-Borne Disease Working Group but does not address whether that Working Group itself continues to be authorized under section 2062 of the 21st Century Cures Act.

The bill adds "increasing capacity to identify, report, prevent, and respond to such diseases" to the CDC national strategy activities but does not specify performance metrics or reporting requirements for that capacity-building.
The bill reauthorizes enhanced support to health departments but does not specify a set-aside for tribal health departments alongside state and local departments.
